title: A new Close waits behind a held reversal of the same work order
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure AccountingHub is enabled for the organization and the test location has no QuickBooks Online connection.
  • Make sure this month's fiscal period, period A, is closed in Accounting.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, closed, with one approved line with one stock part picked from inventory at a cost of $40.00 each, quantity 2, closed last month and posted.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open the Finance tab.
  3. Open the invoice menu on the Finance tab.
  4. Click "Reopen Work Order".
  5. Click Reopen Work Order in the window.
  6. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
  7. Set the posting date to a day of last month.
  8. Click Close Work Order in the confirmation.
  9. Open Accounting > Accounting Events.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The document shows.

Step 3:

  • The menu offers "Reopen Work Order".

Step 4:

  • The window opens.

Step 5:

  • The status reads "Complete".

Step 6:

  • The confirmation opens.

Step 7:

  • The date shows.

Step 8:

  • The work order is Closed again.

Step 9:

  • The reversal shows Held with the reason "Period [period A's name] is closed", dated the reopen date.
  • The new Close shows Held with the reason "Waiting for an earlier held entry of work order [n]".

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as the work order's number or the customer's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11761 (Story 4, Reopen a closed internal or no-charge work order)

  • S4-R3: “Confirming reverses exactly the entries that were posted at Close (Stories 7 and 8), returns the parts to inventory as Reverse does today, removes the internal invoice, and sets the work order to Complete with its classification unchanged, the shop supplies amount kept, and the Convert and Change category actions offered again (S2-R9 applies only while closed or invoiced). The reversal is dated the reopen date, so it is held only if that date's period is closed or missing (S4-E2 is corrected accordingly). Events for one work order are processed in order, one at a time: a Reopen arriving while the Close is Held turns the Close Dismissed; a Dismissed event is never retried and cannot be replayed by hand; a new Close waits while an earlier reversal for the same work order is Held, shown as Held with the reason "Waiting for an earlier held entry of work order [n]", so two Close entries are never posted without the reversal between them. The reversal credits and debits exactly the accounts the Close used.”
  • S4-E2: “If the Close entry was posted in a period that is now closed, the QuickBooks reversal lands in QB Unexported with the closed-period error as today, and the hub holds it with that reason; the work order still reopens.”

From: "Internal Work Orders technical implementation plan", 2026-10-28, last updated 2026-11-10 (revision 5, built on PRD v1.0), sources/TECH-PLAN-Internal-Work-Orders-upload-2026-11-12.md, read 12 Nov 2026

  • Tech plan line 4966 (TP-638): “One empty row, or a period closed at Reopen, holds every later-cycle entry of that work order. Each is visible, names the blocking work order, and releases in order.”
